step1.label: Query analysis
step1.whyDescription: We analyze your question to identify the main topic and classify it correctly. This allows directing the search toward the most relevant committees and parliamentarians.

step2.label: Committees
step2.whyDescription: We identify the most relevant parliamentary committee for the requested topic. Committees are the heart of legislative work: this is where topics are discussed in detail.

step3.label: Authoritative sources
step3.whyDescription: Before retrieving any citation, the system identifies the most authoritative parliamentarians on the topic. Authority is calculated on 6 criteria: floor speeches, legislative acts, committee membership, profession, education and institutional role. Only the most competent voices become priority sources.

step4.label: Speeches
step4.whyDescription: We retrieve speeches from parliamentarians identified as authoritative. This ensures that citations are not random, but come from those who have demonstrated real expertise on the topic.

step5.label: Statistics
step5.whyDescription: We calculate the representation percentages of majority and opposition in the speeches found. This allows us to measure and guarantee the balance of the response.

step6.label: Ideological Compass
step6.whyDescription: We analyze the ideological positioning of parliamentary groups on the specific topic, mapping positions on axes of an ideological compass.

step7.label: Generation
step7.whyDescription: We generate the final balanced synthesis integrating all collected data: speeches, experts, statistics and ideological positioning, with citations verified from parliamentary speeches.

step8.label: Saving
step8.whyDescription: We complete the final verification of the response, validating citations and saving the result to history for future consultation.

profession.label: Profession
profession.description: Contribution of pre-parliamentary profession to the authority score. A parliamentarian with a medical or legal background has specific expertise for sector queries.

education.label: Education
education.description: Contribution of academic qualifications to the authority score. Specialized degrees and PhDs in relevant fields increase the weight.

committee.label: Committees
committee.description: Contribution of membership in thematically relevant parliamentary committees relative to the query. The higher the semantic relevance, the greater the weight.

acts.label: Acts
acts.description: Contribution of the number of parliamentary acts submitted (laws, motions, questions), weighted by recency via exponential time decay.

interventions.label: Speeches
interventions.description: Contribution of the number of floor speeches weighted by recency. Active and recent parliamentarians get higher scores than inactive ones.

role.label: Role
role.description: Contribution of institutional role (President, Minister, Group Leader, Undersecretary, etc.). Top roles receive an authority boost.

relevance.label: Relevance
relevance.description: Weight of the cosine similarity between query embedding and chunk embedding. This is the primary signal of thematic relevance.

diversity.label: Diversity
diversity.description: Penalizes chunks from the same speaker to prevent a single parliamentarian from dominating results, ensuring variety of voices.

coverage.label: Coverage
coverage.description: Rewards representation of multiple parliamentary groups in the final ranking, favoring multi-party perspectives.

authority.label: Authority
authority.description: Re-weights chunks based on the parliamentarian's authority score (expertise, role, acts). Note: the actual authority ranking happens post-merge.

salience.label: Salience
salience.description: Prefers politically substantive texts over procedural ones (e.g., 'Thank you, Mr. President, you may speak').

modelInfo.analyst: Stage 1: decomposes the query into thematic claims per party. Structured and repetitive task — gpt-4o-mini is sufficient and cost-effective.
modelInfo.writer: Stage 2: writes sections for each parliamentary group from retrieved chunks. Requires high narrative quality and ideological coherence.
modelInfo.integrator: Stage 3: integrates sections into a coherent and balanced text. Stage 4 (Citation Surgeon) is deterministic and does not use LLM.

retrieval.title: Information Retrieval
retrieval.description: Parameters for the two search channels and the result merger
retrieval.topKResultsInfo: Maximum number of chunks retrieved by semantic similarity (embedding). Higher values increase recall but also increase latency and computational cost.
retrieval.similarityThresholdInfo: Minimum cosine similarity threshold for the dense channel. Chunks with lower similarity are discarded before ranking. Typical range: 0.20–0.45.
retrieval.minLexicalMatchInfo: Minimum number of EuroVoc keywords that must match lexically to include a parliamentary act in the graph search. Value 1 = one keyword is enough.
retrieval.semanticThresholdInfo: Semantic similarity threshold for EuroVoc matching. Controls how closely the EuroVoc concept must semantically match the query. Typical range: 0.35–0.55.
retrieval.graphChunkThresholdInfo: Minimum similarity threshold for chunks retrieved via graph traversal. Prevents inclusion of off-topic chunks retrieved only through co-signature of relevant acts.
retrieval.maxActsPerQueryInfo: Maximum number of parliamentary acts to retrieve per query via the graph channel. Limits the computational load of Neo4j graph traversal.

authority.title: Authority Score
authority.description: Weights and thresholds for calculating parliamentarian authority scores
authority.halfLifeActsInfo: Half-life in days for temporal decay of parliamentary acts. An act submitted 'half_life' days ago is worth half of a current one. Low values favor recent activity.
authority.halfLifeInterventionsInfo: Half-life in days for temporal decay of floor speeches. Recent speeches weigh more than older ones.
authority.relevanceThresholdsDescription: Minimum cosine similarity between the act/speech embedding and the query. Items below the threshold are excluded from the count, regardless of quantity.
authority.actsRelevanceThresholdInfo: Minimum cosine similarity between the act description and the query to count it toward authority. Irrelevant acts do not contribute to the score. Typical range: 0.20–0.35.
authority.interventionsRelevanceThresholdInfo: Minimum cosine similarity between the speech embedding and the query to count it. Off-topic speeches do not increase the parliamentarian's score. Typical range: 0.20–0.35.
authority.maxComponentContributionInfo: Maximum contribution (cap) that a single component can make to the final authority score. Prevents a single factor (e.g., number of speeches) from completely dominating the score.

generation.title: Generation
generation.description: LLM models and parameters for the 4-stage generation pipeline
generation.maxTokenOutputInfo: Maximum number of tokens generated per response. Increase for longer responses, decrease to contain costs.
generation.temperatureInfo: Model creativity/randomness. 0 = deterministic and precise, 1 = creative and variable. For analytical texts, 0.2–0.4 is optimal.
generation.topPInfo: Nucleus sampling: considers only tokens with cumulative probability up to Top-P. 1.0 = no filtering. Lower to 0.9–0.95 for more focused output.
generation.enabledInfo: Provides the writer with a summary of the parliamentary group's overall position (top N chunks) before writing the section. Improves ideological coherence of selected citations.
generation.maxChunksBriefInfo: Number of chunks included in the position brief. More chunks provide more context but increase input tokens and latency.
generation.charsPerChunkInfo: Maximum characters per chunk in the brief. Truncates long chunks to keep the brief compact.
generation.contextCharsInfo: Context characters shown for each evidence in the brief (text surrounding the citation). Helps the writer understand the tone of the speech.
generation.crossSynthesisInfo: Enables the 'Cross-Party Analysis' section (Stage 3.5): identifies cross-party patterns, convergences and divergences between parliamentary groups. Increases response length and cost.
generation.noEvidenceMessageInfo: Text shown in the parliamentary group section when no relevant speeches are present in the corpus for that query.

queryRewriting.title: Query Rewriting
queryRewriting.description: Automatic expansion of short queries before retrieval
queryRewriting.enabledInfo: When enabled, short queries are reformulated and enriched with related terms before being sent to retrieval. Improves recall for ambiguous or overly concise queries.
queryRewriting.modelInfo: LLM model used to rewrite queries. gpt-4o-mini is recommended: fast, cost-effective and sufficient for this structured task.
queryRewriting.maxWordsInfo: Maximum word threshold: queries with a word count equal to or less than this are rewritten. Already descriptive (longer) queries are passed directly to retrieval.

Privacy.title: Privacy & Legal Notice
Privacy.intro: ParliamentRAG is a non-commercial academic research project. The site uses no analytics, no advertising and no profiling — only technical cookies. Questions you ask in the chat are stored on our server for scientific research purposes.
Privacy.s1b: The data controller is Mirko Tritella (University of Milano-Bicocca research project). For any privacy request contact: privacy@parliamentrag.it.
Privacy.s2b: Chat queries and generated answers are stored on our server to evaluate and improve the system as part of published scientific research. Standard technical logs (e.g. IP addresses in server logs) are kept by our hosting providers for security. Your chat history is also kept locally in your browser (localStorage) and can be cleared by you at any time.
Privacy.s3b: The site sets only strictly necessary, first-party technical cookies: your language preference and interface state (e.g. sidebar). No consent banner is required for such cookies. We use no analytics, advertising or third-party tracking cookies.
Privacy.s4b: Data are processed exclusively for scientific research (system evaluation for peer-reviewed publications) on the basis of legitimate interest for research purposes (art. 6(1)(f) and art. 89 GDPR). Please do not include personal data in your questions: queries are meant to concern parliamentary topics.
Privacy.s5b: Stored conversations are kept for the duration of the research project and its publications, then deleted or irreversibly anonymised.
Privacy.s6b: The knowledge graph contains data about Members of Parliament (names, speeches, votes, careers) sourced from the official open data of the Camera dei Deputati (dati.camera.it), processed in their role as public office holders under the source open licenses.
Privacy.s7b: Answers are generated by artificial intelligence and may contain errors or inaccuracies despite citation verification. ParliamentRAG is an independent research project and is not affiliated with, or endorsed by, the Camera dei Deputati. Always verify quotes against the official record linked in each citation.
Privacy.s8b: The site requires no account and does not link conversations to your identity: stored data are therefore generally anonymous. You can delete a conversation yourself — from our server too — using the trash icon in the chat history. For any other request (access, rectification, or erasure of personal data you may have included in a question) write to privacy@parliamentrag.it. You also retain the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian supervisory authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali).
Privacy.s9b: Below each answer you can leave feedback: a vote, reasons and an optional comment. We store it with a reference to the conversation, without data that identify you, for the research purposes described above. If you want project news and evaluation surveys, you can leave your email address. We process it on the basis of your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). The address does not go into our database: we pass it to Brevo SAS (France, EU), the service that manages the list as our processor (Art. 28 GDPR). Brevo sends you a confirmation email and records the date and IP address of your confirmation as proof of consent. We never link the address to your chat questions or feedback, we do not share it with anyone else, and we do not track email opens or clicks. Every email carries an unsubscribe link: one click and you leave the list. You can also withdraw consent by writing to privacy@parliamentrag.it. When the project ends we delete the whole list. Leaving your email is optional and changes nothing in how you use the site.

DataPage.heroTitle: The knowledge graph behind every answer
DataPage.heroSub: Every deputy, speech, act and vote you read on ParliamentRAG lives in a knowledge graph: a network of facts linked to the open data of the Italian Chamber and the European Union. You can download the whole graph from this page.
DataPage.stTriples: RDF triples in the graph export
DataPage.sec1Note: Sources: open data of the Chamber of Deputies (dati.camera.it) and the EU EuroVoc thesaurus. The graph is updated with every new sitting.
DataPage.idea1Body: A deputy is not a row in a private table: it is an official dati.camera.it URI, the same one the Chamber uses. Whoever cites that address is talking about the same person, with no ambiguity.
DataPage.idea2Body: To say “person”, “organisation”, “topic” we use standard vocabularies — FOAF, W3C ORG, SKOS — instead of inventing our own names. Our data joins with archives, newspapers and researchers without any conversion tables.
DataPage.idea3Body: Knowledge is broken down into minimal subject–predicate–object sentences: “Aiello, is a member of, MoVimento 5 Stelle”. A machine reads them effortlessly and combines them to answer complex questions.
DataPage.sec3Intro: The triples below come straight from the dump: they describe deputy {name}, his record and his group membership.
DataPage.exCaption: Abridged excerpt from the parliamentrag_kg.ttl dump (URIs shortened for readability).
DataPage.ex1Title: The URI is the official one
DataPage.ex1Body: the identifier is the same as dati.camera.it: our data and the Chamber's data link up by themselves.
DataPage.ex2Body: foaf:Person is the standard way of saying “person” on the web of data; ocd:deputato is the Chamber's own open-data vocabulary.
DataPage.ex3Body: group membership is an object with a start and end date (org:Membership): the graph also remembers who switches groups, and when.
DataPage.sec4Title: The same language as official data
DataPage.sec4Intro: Each concept in the graph is aligned to a standard vocabulary. The table is the same one in the paper's appendix, and it is what makes the data readable by any system that knows those vocabularies.
DataPage.r1m: the same official Chamber record, reusable anywhere
DataPage.r2m: the W3C standard for describing organisations
DataPage.r3m: a fact with a start and an end: party switches stay on record
DataPage.r4m: the EU's multilingual thesaurus: the same topics in 24 languages
DataPage.r5m: the structure follows the international standard for parliamentary acts
DataPage.r6m: the open-data vocabulary of the Chamber of Deputies
DataPage.r7m: every build of the graph declares when and from which sources it was made
DataPage.sec5Intro: The whole graph is exported as RDF, the open format of the Semantic Web: readable with any standard tool (Apache Jena, rdflib, GraphDB…) and queryable in SPARQL.

DataPage.fileVotesDesc: The votes cast by each deputy in every electronic ballot of the legislature, one by one.

Method.title: How it works
Method.intro: ParliamentRAG's answers are generated by AI models from the official verbatim records of the Italian Chamber of Deputies (19th legislature). Every quotation is verified word for word against the source; the selection of sources and the synthesis are choices made by the system, governed by the criteria described on this page.
Method.pipelineP1: Each question goes through a staged pipeline: the query is rewritten and expanded, the system retrieves relevant speeches through hybrid semantic search, computes each MP's authority on the topic, generates a section for every parliamentary group and integrates them into a single answer. Quotations are extracted by position from the original text: if a quotation does not match the record, it is discarded.
Method.pipelineP2: The “Behind the scenes” panel available on every answer shows the stages, timings and model calls that produced it.
Method.authorityP1: An MP's authority on a topic is a weighted sum of six components, each between 0 and 1 and computed against the question asked: there is no global score, only a score per topic.
Method.dInterventions: How much, and how recently, they spoke about the topic in the Chamber
Method.dCommittee: Relevance of their committee to the topic
Method.dActs: Acts signed on the topic, weighted by recency
Method.dProfession: Affinity between professional background and topic
Method.dEducation: Affinity between educational background and topic
Method.authorityP2: These weights are an editorial choice, not a neutral measure: they declare which signals count and by how much. We publish them so they can be inspected and challenged; on the <ranking>authority analysis</ranking> page you can change them and watch the ranking shift.
Method.citationsP1: Every quotation is extracted by position from the verbatim record and verified word for word: what appears in quotation marks was actually said, and each quotation links to the official document.
Method.citationsP2: Exactness does not remove selection: which passages to quote, and in what frame, is the system's decision. An authentic quotation can still be partial with respect to the full speech or the speaker's overall position. The full context is always one click away, in the official record.
Method.limitsP1: Answers are generated content and can contain errors or omissions: a relevant speech may not be retrieved, a position may be summarised incompletely. ParliamentRAG is an independent research project, neither affiliated with nor endorsed by the Chamber of Deputies. For anything that matters, check the official record.
Method.linksIntro: The system's architecture, weights and evaluation are documented in the scientific paper:
Method.compassP1: For each question the system generates two thematic axes and asks a language model to classify every retrieved speech: a position between −1 and +1 on each axis, or no position at all. A group's position is the mean of only its speeches that take a stance on that axis, attenuated toward the centre when they are few: a sharp position has to be earned with numbers, not with three sentences.
Method.compassP2: Two reading cautions. A group's coordinates can rest on different sets of speeches for the two axes, and the number of speeches behind each coordinate is shown in the tooltip. Points at the centre take no position: the compass describes what the groups argued in the Chamber on this question, it does not certify their political placement.
